class.name: PhysicsSystem
class.description: [PhysicsSystem] manages the interaction between high-performance ECS entities and Godot's [PhysicsServer3D]. It is engineered to support scenarios with thousands of active physics bodies (e.g., destructible debris, kinematic characters, or hundreds of simultaneous projectiles). The system operates by synchronizing [b]SIMD-aligned transforms[/b] from the [EntityManager] directly to the physics server's internal state. It supports both [b]RigidBody[/b] (server-driven) and [b]Kinematic[/b] (ECS-driven) entities. [b]Performance Highlights:[/b] - [b]Parallel Solver:[/b] Kinematic motion resolution is performed on the [WorkerThreadPool], bypassing the single-threaded bottlenecks of the traditional scene tree. - [b]Direct Table Dispatch:[/b] O(1) correlation between entity IDs and physics server RIDs. - [b]Predictive Sync:[/b] Integrates with Godot's physics interpolation to ensure smooth visual results even at variable frame rates. [b]Note:[/b] To enable physics for an entity, you must attach a [PhysicsBody3DComponent] and register its shape via [method register_entity_physics].

method.name: process_physics_updates
method.description: Synchronizes all entity world transforms from the ECS registry to the [PhysicsServer3D]. [b]Note:[/b] This is normally handled automatically by the [ECSScheduler] during the [NOTIFICATION_PHYSICS_PROCESS] phase. Call this manually only if you need to force a collision update mid-tick.

method.name: register_entity_physics
method.description: Allocates a low-level physics body on the server and attaches it to the entity. The [param mode] determines how the body interacts with the world (static, kinematic, rigid, etc.), using the [enum PhysicsServer3D.BodyMode] enumeration. Once registered, the [PhysicsSystem] will automatically keep the body's transform in sync with the ECS [WorldTransformComponent].

method.name: solve_kinematic_movement_3d
method.description: Performs a high-performance kinematic "Move and Slide" operation for the entity. This method bypasses [CharacterBody3D] logic to perform raw [code]test_motion[/code] calls against the [PhysicsServer3D]. It is highly optimized for mass-character simulations where hundreds of independent AI agents need to navigate a complex collision environment.
